name: Carrion Throne

stars.name: The Vulture
stars.notes: Primary component. High-mass B-class star with powerful stellar wind and significant UV output.

stars.name: The Carrion Bird
stars.notes: Secondary component orbiting at 28 AU. Gravitational interaction with The Vulture perturbs planetary orbits on long timescales.

planets.name: Carcass
planets.notes: Remnant core of a larger body stripped by The Vulture's stellar wind. Dense metallic composition exposed to vacuum—the skeleton of a dead world.

planets.name: Rot
planets.notes: Intense volcanism driven by gravitational perturbation from the binary pair. Sulfurous emissions create a thin, poisonous atmosphere that glows faintly in UV light.

planets.name: The Feast
planets.notes: A gas giant slowly losing its outer atmosphere to The Vulture's radiation pressure. Visible atmospheric stripping creates streamers of gas that trail behind the planet.

planets.name: Bonepicker
planets.notes: Cold, dark world in a wide orbit around the binary barycenter. Surface is fractured permafrost over a dead geological interior. Gravitational perturbation makes its orbit slowly chaotic.

planets.name: Graveworm
planets.notes: Outermost body, barely gravitationally bound to the system. May be a captured object. Surface is ancient dirty ice scarred by cosmic ray impacts over billions of years.

anomalies.name: The Feasting Streamers
anomalies.location: Trailing from The Feast's orbit sunward
anomalies.notes: Diffuse streams of ionized gas stripped from The Feast. Low density but charged enough to cause electrical system interference in passing vessels. Danger level: high.

anomalies.name: Perturbation Cascade
anomalies.location: Between orbits 3 and 5, centered on binary barycenter
anomalies.notes: The binary pair's gravitational interaction creates zones where orbital mechanics become chaotic and unpredictable. Computed trajectories diverge from actual paths within hours. Danger level: extreme for navigation.

anomalies.name: The UV Killing Floor
anomalies.location: Inner system within 5 AU of The Vulture
anomalies.notes: Ultraviolet flux from The Vulture is sufficient to degrade polymer-based hull components and cause rapid photoaging of exposed materials. Danger level: high.

asteroid_belts.name: The Boneyard
asteroid_belts.notes: Dense field of collision fragments. Gravitational perturbation from the binary pair causes periodic orbital resonance pile-ups, creating temporary density spikes that are navigational nightmares.

stations.name: Wraith Corridor Relay 14
stations.location: Far outer system, 80 AU from barycenter
stations.notes: Automated communications relay for the Wraith Corridor deep-space network. Positioned far enough from the binary to avoid perturbation effects. Solar panels supplemented by RTG power.

faction_control.notes: Unclaimed. The system's location along the Wraith Corridor gives it marginal navigational relevance as a relay point, but no territorial value.

history: Carrion Throne was cataloged in 2494 during the Wraith Corridor survey initiative. Initial observations noted the unusual atmospheric stripping of The Feast, visible as luminous streamers in long-exposure imaging.

A prospecting expedition in 2537 entered the system seeking metallic resources in the Boneyard. The expedition vessel 'Bone Dividend' suffered navigational failure in the Perturbation Cascade zone and collided with a Boneyard fragment. The crew was rescued but the vessel was a total loss.

In 2561, astrophysicists determined that Bonepicker's orbit is slowly destabilizing due to binary perturbation. Within approximately 50,000 years, the planet will either be ejected from the system or redirected into the inner system with catastrophic results.
description: Carrion Throne is a binary system where two stars slowly devour their own worlds. The Vulture, a powerful B3V primary, blasts the inner system with ultraviolet radiation and stellar wind strong enough to strip gas from a giant planet. Its companion, The Carrion Bird, contributes gravitational chaos that perturbs orbits and creates navigational dead zones where computed trajectories become fiction. Five worlds orbit this pair in various states of decay—stripped cores, volcanic upheaval, atmospheric hemorrhage, cracking permafrost, and barely-bound ice.

Navigation through Carrion Throne is an exercise in controlled uncertainty. The Perturbation Cascade zone between orbits 3 and 5 makes standard orbital mechanics unreliable; the Boneyard's periodic density spikes can turn a clear path into a debris wall with limited warning; and the Feasting Streamers crossing the inner system cause intermittent electrical interference. The loss of the Bone Dividend demonstrated that even experienced navigators cannot rely on computed trajectories in this system.

The system's one point of value is its position along the Wraith Corridor, a deep-space transit lane connecting two populated sectors. Wraith Corridor Relay 14 maintains communication links through the region from a safe distance. Beyond that automated function, Carrion Throne offers nothing but a slow-motion exhibition of stellar predation—two stars feeding on their own planetary system while the orbits of their remaining worlds gradually deteriorate toward destruction.
